text: Confirmed: in middleware/proxy.go, randomBalancer.Next calls rand.Intn(len(b.targets)) and roundRobinBalancer.Next does b.i % uint32(len(b.targets)) — both panic when the target list is empty. I'm adding empty-list guards so Next returns nil (plus a nil-target guard in the proxy middleware so it doesn't dereference a nil target), then running the full test suite. ETA ~6 min.

Fixed and verified: randomBalancer.Next and roundRobinBalancer.Next now return nil for an empty target list (no more Intn/divide-by-zero panics), and the proxy middleware returns 503 instead of dereferencing a nil target. Full test suite passes (middleware/proxy.go).

Fixed and verified: Router.Find no longer pre-sets ctx.path to the raw request path, so Context#Path() is "" when no route matched (and still the registered route path, e.g. "/users/:id", for matches and 405s). Full test suite passes (router.go).

Fixed and verified: Context#Scheme() now only accepts a valid HTTP scheme ("http"/"https", case-insensitive) from X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Forwarded-Protocol and X-Url-Scheme, in the same precedence order; bogus values like "ftp" are skipped and it falls back to the next header or "http". Full test suite passes (context.go).

Working on it: DefaultBinder.bindData's map branch always sets a single string value, which panics for map[string][]string and gives single strings for map[string]interface{}. I'm making it bind the full value slice for []string / interface{} destinations (first value for map[string]string, converted values for numeric maps). ETA ~3 min.

Working on it: Group.Use registers catch-all NotFoundHandler routes with Any, so a second group with the same prefix overwrites the first group's real routes. I'm switching group middleware catch-alls to a dedicated RouteNotFound pseudo-method (Echo#RouteNotFound / Group#RouteNotFound) that only applies when no handler exists for the request method, so real routes are no longer clobbered. ETA ~3 min.

Working on it: in the Gzip middleware's deferred cleanup, when res.Size == 0 the gzip trailer is discarded but the writer is still closed to the real response, so an empty body still emits gzip bytes while Content-Encoding was deleted. I'm making the empty case finish the gzip stream into the discarded writer so the response stays consistent (valid gzip stream + Content-Encoding: gzip for empty 200 bodies). ETA ~3 min.

Fixed and verified: DefaultBinder now binds maps properly — map[string][]string gets all values per key (no more SetMapIndex panic, nil maps are initialized), map[string]interface{} gets the []string slice, map[string]string keeps the first value, and numeric/bool maps convert values. Full test suite passes (bind.go).

Fixed and verified: group middleware catch-alls now use a new RouteNotFound pseudo-method (Echo#RouteNotFound / Group#RouteNotFound) that is only consulted when no handler exists for the request method, so a second group with the same prefix no longer overwrites the first group's routes. GET /group runs the first group's handler with m1, GET /group/other runs the second group's route with m2, and 405 handling for normal routes is unchanged. Full test suite passes (router.go, echo.go, group.go).
